version: as published with LiTraj (repository pushed_at 2025-06-05; paper npj Comput. Mater. 11, 131, 2025)
paper_reference: Dembitskiy et al., "Benchmarking machine learning models for predicting lithium ion migration", npj Computational Materials 11, 131 (2025)
record_unit: one Li-ion vacancy-hop (edge) between two equilibrium sites, with a BVSE-NEB migration barrier
available_structure_fields: supercell with a dummy centroid ('X') atom marking the hop midpoint, per edge, in extended-XYZ (nebBVSE122k_train/val/test.xyz)

target_fields.em: BVSE-NEB migration barrier for this hop, eV

known_missing_censored_disordered_data: No missing em values (0/122421). No censored values (empirical BVSE barrier, always numeric). 0 duplicate edge_id rows (verified). Disorder of underlying structures not separately re-verified in this phase; supercell + centroid representation must be handled explicitly by the feature/graph builder in Phase 1.
notes: material_id set (11,290 unique materials) is an exact subset of bvel_percolation's material_id set (12,807), and dft_neb's material_id set (867) is an exact subset of this dataset's (see reports/results/leakage/pretraining_id_overlap.json). Multiple edges (average ~10.8) exist per material, corresponding to distinct candidate hops for the same crystal.
